title: RSI exam
description: Rapid sequence intubation: indications, preoxygenation, RSI medicines and their order, care after the tube.

answers: When the patient cannot protect the airway (GCS ≤ 8, snoring breathing) or does not improve on oxygen
For every unconscious patient, even if they breathe well and the SpO2 is normal on oxygen
When the patient is agitated and fights the mask, so that the oxygen can be given safely
For severe pain that Fentanyl does not relieve, so the patient can be sedated deeply

questions.q: What is the correct order of RSI?
answers: Preoxygenation → Ketamine → Rocuronium → intubation → ventilation with oxygen
Preoxygenation → Rocuronium → Ketamine → intubation → ventilation with oxygen
Ketamine → Rocuronium → preoxygenation → intubation → ventilation with oxygen
Preoxygenation → Ketamine → intubation → Rocuronium → ventilation with oxygen
About 3 minutes of oxygen on a mask before RSI
About 3 minutes of oxygen through the tube after RSI
A few fast bag breaths right before the Rocuronium
About 30 seconds of oxygen on a mask after the Ketamine
After the paralysis the patient does not breathe and the SpO2 falls fast
It calms the patient, so less Ketamine is needed for the induction
It makes Rocuronium work faster, so the tube can go in sooner
It raises the blood pressure before the Ketamine lowers it

questions.q: What happens shortly after giving Rocuronium?
answers: The patient's own breathing stops, they must be ventilated
The patient falls asleep, but keeps breathing on their own
The breathing slows a little, the mask is still enough
Nothing until Ketamine is given, then the breathing stops

questions.q: What is the RSI dose of Rocuronium?
answers: 1–1.2 mg/kg
1.5–2 mg/kg
1–1.2 mcg/kg

questions.q: What is the RSI dose of Ketamine?
answers: 1.5 mg/kg
0.3 mg/kg
1.2 mg/kg
0.15 mg/kg

questions.q: Why is Ketamine the induction agent prehospitally?
answers: It keeps the blood pressure, safe even in shock
It also relaxes the muscles, so less Rocuronium
Naloxone reverses it if the intubation fails
It works the longest, so no repeat dose is needed

questions.q: What is needed for an intubated patient to be oxygenated well?
answers: Continuous ventilation with oxygen through the tube
An oxygen mask over the face, the tube keeps it open
Ventilation through the tube only when the SpO2 falls
Oxygen through the tube, the patient breathes alone

questions.q: The oxygen of an intubated patient runs out. What happens?
answers: The ventilation does not work and the SpO2 falls: change the oxygen source at once
Nothing for about an hour, the oxygen reserve from preoxygenation is enough
The patient starts breathing alone through the tube, so the SpO2 stays stable
The SpO2 falls slowly: you can finish the transport and change it in hospital
About 40–60 minutes
About 5–10 minutes
About 2–3 hours
About 1–2 minutes

questions.q: Why do we not give Rocuronium without sedation?
answers: The patient stays conscious, paralysed and suffocating
Without Ketamine it does not reach the muscles at all
It causes a dangerous rise of the blood pressure alone
It would wear off within a minute without the sedative

questions.q: Burned patient: soot around the mouth, hoarse voice, difficult breathing. What do you do?
answers: Early intubation, because the airway swells fast
Oxygen mask and watch, intubate only if SpO2 falls
No intubation: the burned airway would bleed
Salbutamol nebulised to open the swollen airway

questions.q: Which breathing shows that an unconscious patient does not protect the airway?
answers: Snoring
Deep and fast
Wheezing
Slow but regular

questions.q: What is the role of Fentanyl in RSI?
answers: Optional: it dulls the stress of intubation, but lowers breathing and blood pressure
Mandatory: it is the induction agent if Ketamine is not available on the vehicle
Mandatory: it is always given first, before the Ketamine, for pain relief
Optional: it replaces Rocuronium when the patient is already unconscious

questions.q: What do you do after a successful intubation?
answers: Continuous oxygen, monitoring (SpO2, rhythm), transport
Oxygen until the SpO2 is 100%, then stop the ventilation
Remove the monitor, the tube is enough for safe transport
Wait on scene until the Rocuronium wears off, then transport
Severe loss of consciousness: the patient probably cannot protect the airway
Moderate confusion: the patient answers, but the airway is still protected
Mild confusion: the patient is awake, oxygen on a mask is enough for now
Normal consciousness after a head injury, but the patient must be watched

questions.q: The intubation fails and the SpO2 is falling. What do you do?
answers: Stop, oxygenate with the mask, then try again
Keep trying, the tube is the fastest way to oxygen
Give another dose of Rocuronium, then try again
Give Adrenaline to raise the SpO2, then try again
